title: Basic Templates
objective: Learn what fabrication templates are, why different template types and materials are used, and how approved job information gives a template its meaning.
safety_boundary: Learning only. This lesson is for recognising and understanding templates. It does not authorise practical marking-out, cutting, forming, machine operation or hazardous fabrication activity. Practical work requires approved training, workplace controls and competent human supervision.

sections.heading: What is a fabrication template?
sections.body: A fabrication template is a controlled reference used to represent a required shape, outline, position or relationship for a component. Its meaning comes from the approved drawing, specification or other controlled job information.

sections.heading: Why are there different kinds of templates?
sections.body: Different jobs can require different template forms. The correct template type depends on the controlled job requirement, not guesswork or convenience.

sections.heading: Template materials
sections.body: Templates may be made from different suitable materials depending on the workplace requirement, durability needed, accuracy expected and how the reference will be controlled or reused.

sections.heading: What information gives a template meaning?
sections.body: A template should be linked to the correct job, drawing or specification. Controlled information can include identity, orientation, dimensions, reference points, revision status and the component or feature represented.

sections.heading: Basic marking-off principles at knowledge level
sections.body: Marking-off is the controlled transfer or representation of job information so that positions, outlines or reference features can be understood before fabrication. Practical marking-out belongs in supervised practical training.

sections.heading: How templates fit into fabrication planning
sections.body: Templates help connect drawing information to a planned component or feature. Check that the template belongs to the correct job and current controlled information.
